- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% to prevent overreaction.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.5) within 5 days, model frequently underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to counteract sentiment-driven sell-off bias.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day forecasts when sentiment is mixed or trending downward; apply a 0.5–1.5% upward bias to capture sentiment-driven rebound.
- In low-volatility periods (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days of flat or slightly rising prices), model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% to reflect momentum.
